newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Continental to resume Venezuela flights.
newsitem.headline: Continental to resume Venezuela flights.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc will resume direct flights to Venezuela Oct. 1, after an absence of 15 years, with service between Houston and Caracas, company officials said Tuesday.

The new route is aimed at capitalizing on the important oil and petrochemicals links opening up between the two cities, Ralph Shulz, vice-president of sales and marketing for Latin America, told a news conference.
Continental plans to add a New York-Caracas service in 1998, Andrew Czobor, director of planning and strategy for Latin America, said.
The Caracas-Houston route should carry an average of 104 passengers per day and turn a profit of about $5.6 million per year, Czobor said.
Caracas will be Continental's 26th destination in Latin America and the company plans to add a New York-Sao Paulo-Rio de Janeiro route July 10, company officials said.
